title: CREATE DATABASE
description: Create a MySQL database with deliberate text defaults, understand session targeting and privileges, and detect configuration drift without assuming IF NOT EXISTS repairs it.
notes:
## Creation establishes a named database container

CREATE DATABASE introduces a named database on the connected server. In MySQL, that database groups objects such as tables and views and carries defaults used when objects are created without their own explicit settings. It does not populate a complete application, copy an existing dataset, or automatically give every account permission to read the new objects.

For a campus reporting project, campus_reporting is a meaningful database name, while students is a likely table inside it. The difference matters because creating the database does not create the students table. Describe the intended object level before writing SQL: server connection, database container, table definition, and rows represent different decisions and different operations.

## State the target dialect before using the syntax

In MySQL, CREATE SCHEMA is a synonym for CREATE DATABASE. A script using CREATE SCHEMA campus_reporting does not introduce an additional namespace inside the current MySQL database. It creates the same kind of database container. PostgreSQL instead has schemas inside a database, so importing a namespace-oriented script without checking the dialect can change its meaning.

PostgreSQL database creation also has its own supported options and execution restrictions. In particular, CREATE DATABASE cannot execute inside a transaction block. Do not generalize that restriction into a claim that all database systems implement DDL identically. The executable exercises here target MySQL-style syntax, while the comparisons identify why an engine-specific reading is necessary.

## Choose stable names and quote identifiers correctly

Use a clear naming convention with consistent lowercase spelling and a documented environment suffix when appropriate. A database name is an identifier, not a text value. In ordinary MySQL syntax, backticks quote identifiers; single quotes denote strings in expressions. Avoid making generated identifiers from unchecked input or treating value-parameter binding as automatic support for arbitrary identifier substitution.

Case behaviour for MySQL database and table names depends on the platform and relevant server configuration. A spelling that works on one development machine can fail after transfer to another setup. Consistent spelling reduces this risk, but a migration still needs verification on its actual target. Do not infer identifier rules from the collation used for stored student names.

## Text defaults deserve an explicit decision

A character set determines the supported character representation, while a collation supplies comparison and ordering rules for character data. A database can define defaults inherited by new tables when their definitions do not override those choices. That inheritance is a convenience, not a promise that every existing column always matches the latest database default.

The example chooses utf8mb4 and a named supported collation deliberately. Different MySQL versions and compatible products can support different collation names and semantics. A local MariaDB run is therefore recorded separately from exact MySQL verification. Choose a collation for the application's equality and sorting needs rather than copying a name solely because it worked in a tutorial fixture.

```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS campus_reporting
  DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8mb4
  COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;
```

## Creating a database does not select it

The current default database is a session setting. CREATE DATABASE does not automatically change that setting. In MySQL, USE campus_reporting changes the default database for subsequent unqualified object references in that connection. An explicitly qualified name such as campus_reporting.students can also identify the intended object without changing the default database.

This distinction corrects an easy misconception: a new connection is not always required before creating a MySQL table in another database. The connection must have appropriate access and must target the object correctly. Other products use different connection and cross-database rules, so a portable explanation should identify the product instead of saying every engine requires the same switch operation.

## IF NOT EXISTS handles a name collision only

If the requested name already exists, IF NOT EXISTS avoids the ordinary already-exists error for that creation statement. It does not compare the existing database with the proposed definition and reconcile differences. A database created earlier with another collation can retain that setting even when the repeated CREATE statement requests the new default.

That is why a provisioning workflow needs an inspection step. Query the relevant catalog metadata and compare the observed defaults with the expected contract. Report a mismatch rather than assuming successful command completion proves configuration agreement. Changing defaults, converting existing data, and checking application compatibility are separate tasks with different consequences; the exercises do not silently perform those changes.

## Inspect the object that was actually created

INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA exposes database metadata visible to the current account. Selecting the intended schema name, default character set and default collation makes the result more informative than merely seeing an acknowledgment. Keep the filter specific to the database being checked so unrelated system or application databases do not enter the report.

Catalog visibility is also subject to access rules. An account seeing no matching catalog row should not automatically conclude the database is absent for every administrator. The verification task needs the correct connection, account and expected visibility. Likewise, observing an object does not establish that the application account has all the permissions needed for its later workload.

## Separate provisioning authority from application use

Creating a database requires the relevant MySQL privilege. A runtime account that can query selected application tables does not necessarily have permission to create another database, and it should not be described as broken merely because provisioning fails. Establish which actor owns that operation and which account the application will use afterward.

Database creation is not an authorization shortcut. It does not make tenant isolation automatic or validate that a caller should see every table in the container. Object privileges and trusted application checks still govern access. These notes explain the operation; they do not recommend granting broad administrative authority to a normal exercise runner or to a browser-facing application account.

## Cross-database references follow product boundaries

On a MySQL server, supported qualified table references can read objects from different databases in one query when the account has appropriate access. A blanket statement that ordinary joins across databases always need an external connector is inaccurate for that setting. Accessing another server introduces a different connectivity problem and cannot be inferred from a local database-qualified name.

PostgreSQL normally connects a session to one database, with its schemas providing namespaces inside that connection. Additional cross-database mechanisms have their own configuration and semantics. Keep these contrasts scoped: knowing that one MySQL qualified join is possible does not prove every product, hosted service or cross-server arrangement offers the same capability.

## Verification should include the already-existing case

The introductory exercise creates a specifically named disposable database with explicit defaults, builds a temporary table inside it, and copies supplied labels into that table. The result reports the observed catalog defaults and copied count. Empty input still requires the definition, while repeated labels still count as separate supplied occurrences under the stated input contract.

The second exercise starts from a deliberately existing database. It attempts the same guarded creation and reports whether the observed defaults agree with the requested ones. One fixture begins with an older text default so that a mismatch remains visible. Neither exercise treats IF NOT EXISTS as an ALTER DATABASE operation, and neither needs production records or credentials.

## Treat creation and operational completion separately

A successful CREATE DATABASE statement is one step in a broader lifecycle. Table definitions, compatible constraints, data loading, account permissions, application configuration and recovery procedures still require their own decisions. Avoid claiming a new database is ready for every workload merely because its name appears in a catalog. Likewise, deleting a database is a separate destructive operation, not an automatic response to a failed configuration comparison.

The exercise outputs verify observable results under their supplied setup. They do not prove every student submission used the required DDL, and a sandbox that forbids database creation cannot execute them without an appropriate administrative lab. Keep that runner capability requirement explicit. Local compatibility results, exact MySQL execution, hosted-provider support and application migration application remain distinct verification claims.

questions.question_text: What does CREATE DATABASE establish in MySQL?
options: To add a new column to an existing table
A named database container with defaults for objects created within it
To generate a new row of data
To create an index on a table
questions.explanation: MySQL database and schema are synonymous; there is no extra required inner schema level.

questions.question_text: Which execution restriction applies to PostgreSQL CREATE DATABASE?
options: It requires two-phase commit
It cannot execute inside a transaction block
It is deprecated syntax
It always requires superuser privileges
questions.explanation: This is a product-defined execution restriction, not a general claim about every DDL implementation.

questions.question_text: What should precede a database-removal decision after a defaults mismatch?
options: The database must contain at least one table
A separate explicit review of the target, dependent data and operation consequences
The database must be renamed first
All tables must be truncated first
questions.explanation: A configuration mismatch does not authorize deletion; active-session restrictions differ by engine.

questions.question_text: In MySQL, what is the relationship between CREATE DATABASE and CREATE SCHEMA?
options: CREATE SCHEMA creates a namespace inside a database created by CREATE DATABASE
They are unrelated commands
CREATE SCHEMA is only used for views
They are exact synonyms — both create the same kind of object
questions.explanation: MySQL treats 'schema' and 'database' as synonyms, unlike PostgreSQL/SQL Server/Oracle where schema is a namespace inside a database.

questions.question_text: How can a MySQL connection target a newly created database for table creation?
options: Nothing, tables can be created from any connection
Restart the database server
Select it with USE or use an appropriately qualified object name with the required privileges
Grant themselves superuser rights
questions.explanation: CREATE DATABASE does not change the default database; a new connection is not inherently necessary.

questions.question_text: In MySQL, which clause avoids the already-existing-database error for guarded creation?
options: CASCADE
IF NOT EXISTS
WITH CHECK OPTION
ON CONFLICT
questions.explanation: The existing database is not reconciled with a changed proposed definition.

questions.question_text: Can MySQL join permitted tables in two databases on the same server using qualified names?
options: JOIN syntax does not support more than one table
Yes; appropriate database-qualified names and access can support this directly
Databases cannot contain more than one table each
SQL does not support JOIN at all
questions.explanation: Do not confuse MySQL database namespaces with PostgreSQL cross-database connectivity.

questions.question_text: A team creates a database on a case-insensitive Windows file system and later deploys the same script on a Linux server. What subtle issue can arise?
options: Linux does not support CREATE DATABASE
Database name case sensitivity differs between operating systems, potentially causing name-mismatch bugs
SQL syntax differs entirely between operating systems
Windows does not allow more than one database
questions.explanation: Case sensitivity of database names can differ by OS/file system, which is a real cross-environment migration pitfall.

questions.question_text: Does CREATE DATABASE also create a students table automatically?
options: Yes, with default columns
No
Only if the name contains campus
Only with utf8mb4
questions.explanation: Container creation and table definition are separate operations.

questions.question_text: What does a database default collation primarily influence?
options: All existing columns are rewritten automatically
Every account gains access
Defaults for newly created objects that do not override it
Identifier case rules become identical everywhere
questions.explanation: Default inheritance does not retroactively convert existing columns.

questions.question_text: An existing database uses latin1. Does IF NOT EXISTS with utf8mb4 repair it?
options: Yes, including every stored value
Only if the SELECT is sorted
No
Only when the name is lowercase
questions.explanation: A name collision is not a configuration reconciliation operation.

questions.question_text: Which MySQL statement changes a connection’s default database?
options: CREATE TABLE alone
SELECT DISTINCT alone
ORDER BY alone
USE database_name
questions.explanation: Creation does not select the new context.

questions.question_text: Why inspect SCHEMATA after guarded creation?
options: To compare observed database defaults with the intended settings
To grant every user privileges
To copy every table
To prove all workloads are fast
questions.explanation: Successful completion alone does not prove existing settings agree.

questions.question_text: Which MySQL quoting convention ordinarily denotes an identifier?
options: Single-quoted text values
Backticks
A GPA decimal literal
An unescaped input string concatenated arbitrarily
questions.explanation: Identifiers and values have different syntax and validation requirements.

questions.question_text: Does database creation grant every account access automatically?
options: Yes, including anonymous callers
Only for student tables
No
Only if it is called schema
questions.explanation: Privileges remain a separate access boundary.

questions.question_text: What can make a supported collation name differ between products?
options: The number of labels copied
An output alias
The row ordering alone
The actual engine and version
questions.explanation: Compatibility products do not necessarily expose the exact same collation inventory.

questions.question_text: Why can a catalog query return no visible database row?
options: The target may be absent or not visible to that account
Every database must be empty
The server has no privileges system
CREATE DATABASE always failed globally
questions.explanation: Interpret observations within connection and actor scope.

questions.question_text: Does a same-server qualified reference establish remote-server access?
options: Yes, automatically
No
Only with DISTINCT
Only with uppercase names
questions.explanation: Cross-server connectivity is a separate problem.

questions.question_text: Which account is appropriate for an administrative creation lab?
options: Every production application account
Any anonymous browser user
One explicitly authorized for the isolated provisioning operation
An account whose denial is bypassed
questions.explanation: Runner capability is a requirement, not a reason to widen ordinary access.

questions.question_text: What does a copied-label count verify?
options: That arbitrary student code used CREATE DATABASE
Every provider supports the operation
All access rules are correct
The supplied copy result in that exercise setup
questions.explanation: Recorded output checks have a limited observable scope.

coding_problems.title: Create a disposable database with explicit text defaults
coding_problems.task: In an authorized administrative lab, create database cx_dbms_lab_catalog if absent, with utf8mb4 and utf8mb4_unicode_ci defaults. Create TEMPORARY table cx_dbms_lab_catalog.copied_labels(label VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL), copy labels from supplied lab_labels, and return database_name, character_set_name, collation_name and label_count. The database is initially absent or already has those exact defaults. Do not execute this against application databases.
coding_problems.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE lab_labels (label VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL);
coding_problems.expected:
database_name	character_set_name	collation_name	label_count
cx_dbms_lab_catalog	utf8mb4	utf8mb4_unicode_ci	2
coding_problems.ordering: Exactly one catalog row for the stated database.
constraints: Requires CREATE DATABASE in an isolated administrative lab; restricted query runners may not support it.
Only cx_dbms_lab_catalog is the creation target.
edge_cases: Empty labels still creates the requested structure.
Repeated input labels count as separate occurrences.
hints: Create the database with explicit defaults before the qualified temporary table.
Inspect INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMATA for the named target.
coding_problems.solution_sql: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS cx_dbms_lab_catalog DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci; CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE cx_dbms_lab_catalog.copied_labels (label VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL); INSERT INTO cx_dbms_lab_catalog.copied_labels SELECT label FROM lab_labels; SELECT SCHEMA_NAME AS database_name,DEFAULT_CHARACTER_SET_NAME AS character_set_name,DEFAULT_COLLATION_NAME AS collation_name,(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cx_dbms_lab_catalog.copied_labels) AS label_count FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA WHERE SCHEMA_NAME='cx_dbms_lab_catalog';
coding_problems.explanation: Database defaults and qualified table placement are explicit; catalog output and copied count expose the resulting definition and state.

validation_cases.expected:
database_name	character_set_name	collation_name	label_count
cx_dbms_lab_catalog	utf8mb4	utf8mb4_unicode_ci	0

database_name	character_set_name	collation_name	label_count
cx_dbms_lab_catalog	utf8mb4	utf8mb4_unicode_ci	3

coding_problems.title: Detect defaults drift after guarded database creation
coding_problems.task: The isolated fixture prepares cx_dbms_lab_existing. Attempt CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS with utf8mb4 and utf8mb4_unicode_ci, then compare the actual catalog defaults with requested_defaults. Return database_name and defaults_match as 1 only when both defaults match. Do not alter the existing database or remove it. The fixture setup deliberately selects the initial defaults for each case.
coding_problems.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE requested_defaults (character_set_name VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL, collation_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);
coding_problems.seed_sql: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS cx_dbms_lab_existing; ALTER DATABASE cx_dbms_lab_existing CHARACTER SET latin1 COLLATE latin1_swedish_ci; INSERT INTO requested_defaults VALUES ('utf8mb4','utf8mb4_unicode_ci');
constraints: Administrative lab only; fixed disposable database name.
The solution must not repair or remove an existing database.
edge_cases: Existing latin1 defaults remain a mismatch.
hints: IF NOT EXISTS does not change existing defaults.
Compare both observed attributes rather than only the database name.
coding_problems.solution_sql: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS cx_dbms_lab_existing DEFAULT CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci; SELECT s.SCHEMA_NAME AS database_name,(s.DEFAULT_CHARACTER_SET_NAME=r.character_set_name AND s.DEFAULT_COLLATION_NAME=r.collation_name) AS defaults_match FROM information_schema.SCHEMATA s CROSS JOIN requested_defaults r WHERE s.SCHEMA_NAME='cx_dbms_lab_existing';
coding_problems.explanation: Guarded creation preserves existing defaults; the report exposes agreement rather than silently changing an existing object.

validation_cases.seed_sql: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS cx_dbms_lab_existing; ALTER DATABASE cx_dbms_lab_existing CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci; INSERT INTO requested_defaults VALUES ('utf8mb4','utf8mb4_unicode_ci');

CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS cx_dbms_lab_existing; ALTER DATABASE cx_dbms_lab_existing CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_bin; INSERT INTO requested_defaults VALUES ('utf8mb4','utf8mb4_unicode_ci');

original_questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the CREATE DATABASE statement?
options: To add a new column to an existing table
To provision a new top-level container that holds schemas, tables, and its own storage
To generate a new row of data
To create an index on a table
original_questions.explanation: CREATE DATABASE provisions a brand-new top-level container with its own catalog metadata and storage.

original_questions.question_text: In PostgreSQL, why can't CREATE DATABASE normally be run inside a BEGIN...COMMIT transaction block?
options: It requires two-phase commit
It involves file-system-level allocation that isn't easily made transactional
It is deprecated syntax
It always requires superuser privileges
original_questions.explanation: Creating a database allocates physical files/storage, an operation PostgreSQL does not allow inside a regular transaction.

original_questions.question_text: Which of the following must generally be true before DROP DATABASE will succeed on most engines?
options: The database must contain at least one table
No active sessions can be connected to that database
The database must be renamed first
All tables must be truncated first
original_questions.explanation: Most engines refuse to drop a database while other sessions are still connected to it.

original_questions.question_text: In MySQL, what is the relationship between CREATE DATABASE and CREATE SCHEMA?
options: CREATE SCHEMA creates a namespace inside a database created by CREATE DATABASE
They are unrelated commands
CREATE SCHEMA is only used for views
They are exact synonyms — both create the same kind of object
original_questions.explanation: MySQL treats 'schema' and 'database' as synonyms, unlike PostgreSQL/SQL Server/Oracle where schema is a namespace inside a database.

original_questions.question_text: What must a client do immediately after creating a new database before creating tables in it?
options: Nothing, tables can be created from any connection
Restart the database server
Connect to (switch into) the newly created database
Grant themselves superuser rights
original_questions.explanation: You must connect to the new database before you can create objects inside it — CREATE DATABASE alone does not switch your session's context.

original_questions.question_text: Which clause prevents an error when CREATE DATABASE is run against a name that may already exist?
options: CASCADE
IF NOT EXISTS
WITH CHECK OPTION
ON CONFLICT
original_questions.explanation: IF NOT EXISTS makes the statement a no-op instead of erroring when the database name is already taken.

original_questions.question_text: Why is directly running SQL JOINs across two separate databases on the same server typically not possible without special setup?
options: JOIN syntax does not support more than one table
Databases are isolated units; cross-database access needs mechanisms like linked servers, dblink, or foreign data wrappers
Databases cannot contain more than one table each
SQL does not support JOIN at all
original_questions.explanation: Databases are designed as isolated containers, so cross-database querying needs special connectivity features rather than a plain JOIN.

original_questions.question_text: A team creates a database on a case-insensitive Windows file system and later deploys the same script on a Linux server. What subtle issue can arise?
options: Linux does not support CREATE DATABASE
Database name case sensitivity differs between operating systems, potentially causing name-mismatch bugs
SQL syntax differs entirely between operating systems
Windows does not allow more than one database
original_questions.explanation: Case sensitivity of database names can differ by OS/file system, which is a real cross-environment migration pitfall.
